title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-22
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 3NT. West's lead is won in the dummy. South has 6 top tricks (3 spades, the ♥A, the ♦A, and the ♣A). Playing on diamonds will risk defeat when that suit is 5-2. It seems that South should play on clubs, but there are serious entry problems.

If South cashes the ♣A and continues with the ♣Q, the defense might be able to duck this trick. South lacks the hand entries to establish and cash his long clubs. At the same time, dummy now lacks the entries to establish and cash the diamonds.

South can guarantee the contract by leading the ♣Q before cashing the ♣A. As before, the defense must duck (if the defense wins and plays hearts, South can discard the ♣A on a top spade). After the ♣Q holds, South switches to diamonds, conceding a trick to the ♦K. The ♣A is an entry to the dummy, and the ♥A is an entry to the closed hand. South will score 3 spade tricks, the ♥A, at least 3 diamond tricks, and 2 club tricks.
